Each specialist repeats all the adjacency bonuses of its tile and costs Food and Happiness (more each age), so specialists only go where a tile's adjacency pays for them. The plan counts on this share of each city's specialist limit on such tiles, so it gathers buildings with high adjacency on the same tiles. Towns have no specialists.

Every new settlement starts as a town. A future city needs room and production to grow big; a town you keep grows to population 7, then sends all its food to connected cities (by road, or both on the coast of the same continent) and turns its production into gold. «Both» scores every site for both jobs and keeps the better one.

When a city grows and the game asks where the new citizen goes, mark the best new tile by your priorities (green), the tiles the building plan needs, and the specialist tile that gains most (blue). The one that wins overall says «best choice». Numbers are value per turn by your priority; a specialist's is after the food and happiness it costs (the game's red numbers), which count for less when the city has plenty to spare and for more when it would run short. A tile where the building plan puts a building («a building comes here») counts only until that turn. The choice stays yours.

Autopilot is ON: it acts at the start of each of your turns

While on, at the start of each of your turns the autopilot makes the decisions ticked below with the game's own commands (it works online too). It moves units only with the unit options below. It switches off when the game is loaded again.
Run the ticked decisions once right now (does not end the turn).
For stepping away (for example online with a turn timer): research, policies and other choices, production, growth, towns and purchases are decided for you; units move only if you tick their options.
When nothing is being researched, pick the game advisor's recommendation (the one matching your priority first), as the tech and civics choosers show it.

A city whose queue is empty gets its next two planned buildings on their planned tiles; if the plan has nothing buildable there, the advisor's top choice (a building on the tile the game rates best, a project, or a military unit).
A grown city places its new citizen where the growth hints say «best choice»: a new tile or a specialist.

A Growing town at population 7+ that is connected to a city takes the recommended Focus; before that, its new citizens favour tiles that suit it (farms for a farming town, mines for a mining town). A Focus already chosen is never changed. While towns outnumber cities, the best town becomes a city (a town founded on a city site first; with the science or economic focus the one with the most production); after that, only a town the Towns tab rates «convert» on its yields. The gold is saved for it: other purchases wait until it is converted.

Buy up to 3 planned buildings per turn, best value per gold first, then upgrade up to 3 military units the game allows to upgrade (those near a threatened settlement first), always keeping the reserve below. Towns' buildings (warehouses) take at most half the spare gold, and none while gold is saved for a goal.
Units waiting for orders skip this turn (they are not moved), so the turn can end.
End the turn when done, so nobody waits for the timer. Not while the game still waits for a choice the autopilot does not make: the log then names it.

Purchases keep this many turns of your gold income in the treasury, at most 1000 gold (late in the game a few turns of income would leave thousands idle). With a negative income: 10 turns of the deficit. The gold for a savings goal (a town conversion; with the victory focus, the path's next building) is held too: smaller purchases wait until it is bought. Repairs, walls and defenders under threat use all the gold. With «Strategy by phase» (and the victory focus) the phase sets the reserve for each turn instead (its tooltip in the strategy line); this setting stays as you chose it.

Recalculate the building plan for all settlements this often (and at once after a building is finished, a tile is gained or new buildings unlock). Fast: only changed settlements are re-planned. Your building tacks are updated too if you placed them.
Experimental: hands your whole civilization, units included, to the game's own AI for that many turns, then gives it back. Only in single-player games.
The AI also moves units and may start or end wars. It stops after the chosen turns, one turn before the age ends (you choose the next civilization), when someone wins, or if you are defeated.
Not available in multiplayer: use the autopilot above.

The game is playing your civilization by itself: an age changed during an earlier AI run, and the game saved your place as an AI player. «Take back control» asks the game to return it after one turn.

When a city's queue is empty, start the wonder the Wonders tab rates best for it: a race you are likely to win that finishes before the age ends, best value per turn of production (its yields, the boost to neighbouring buildings, and its worth for the culture legacy path and Tourism). At most this many wonders in production at once, each on its best tile.

Makes the choices that hold the turn: empty policy slots (the card worth most by Policy Yield Previews when that mod is installed, else the first offered), the celebration bonus, story events (the option the game's AI prefers), a pantheon, a religion and its beliefs (worth most by Policy Yield Previews first), a government, a city-state bonus, the greeting for a newly met leader (friendly when allowed, else neutral), a leader's proposal (the cheapest answer that is not a rejection; never a rejection, which can mean war), "seen it" screens and advisor warnings. Espionage notices («Espionage revealed») are read. Great works waiting in the archive are put on display in free slots. An ally's call to arms is never joined (that is a surprise war, with war weariness): it is set aside, and declined (the alliance ends) only if the game still holds the turn for it. Peace (nothing given or asked) is proposed to every leader at war with you, every 3 turns.

Scouts head for the nearest discovery (cave, ruins, campfire...) within 4 turns first, even while exploring by themselves, then explore (the game's automatic exploring, else the edge of the fog). Cities train scouts first until you have 2. In the Modern age explorers dig up artifacts (ruins, natural wonders) and research new dig sites at your museums and universities; up to 2 are trained while there is something to dig or research.

Cities train settlers (2 at a time while you have fewer than 3 settlements, then 1, never past the settlement cap; they go to the front of the queue). A settler waiting for orders walks to the best free site of the Settlements tab (searched by itself every 5 turns; the role that keeps cities and towns 1 to 1 first, else the game's suggestion), at most 10 turns away, and founds a settlement there; a town founded on a city site becomes a city when gold allows. Each settler gets its own site; no move may start a war. Settlers keep away from hostile military units: no site with one within 3 tiles, no way passing within 2; with one within 3, a settler stays in or runs to your nearest settlement (or steps away), even while walking; in a settlement it leaves for a safe site when its whole way there stays more than 3 tiles from them, else for another of your settlements with no enemies near. No site closer than 5 tiles to another player's settlement, nor within 3 tiles of an independent's village, nor within 6 of any village, friendly or not (founding there makes it hostile). A settler that has walked 12 turns, or changed its site 3 times, takes the nearest safe site. No settler is trained while no site is known. In the Antiquity age, below the settlement cap, no new wonder or science project starts: settlers first. A Migrant joins the settlement it stands in (Resettle; city or town), else walks to your nearest one, its citizen on the tile the growth hints rate best. In the Exploration age, until Shipbuilding, no land unit is sent across deep ocean (it stops on every ocean tile and takes damage there); coast is fine.

A military unit waiting for orders disperses an independent's village it stands on; else shoots (ranged units) at an enemy soldier next to your settlements first, then at other soldiers, the most damaged first (never at an empty tile, never a shot that would start a war); else heals when hurt; else walks onto an empty village at war with you within 4 tiles to disperse it (not a garrison; not while someone befriends it); else fortifies (or stands guard) where it stands. A melee unit (a fortified one too) attacks a hostile unit next to it near your settlements when the game's own combat preview says it clearly wins: the enemy dies or takes twice the damage it deals, and your unit keeps at least half its health; never an attack on a settlement, never one that starts a war. A settlement is threatened with 2+ hostile units within 4 tiles, or one within 2, or one within 4 while its centre is damaged (only independents at war with you count, and not a village's own units standing by it unless they are next to the settlement or attacking it): while it has fewer of your soldiers around it than hostile units, it buys its strongest melee unit at once with all the gold (towns too), the nearest city trains one first, soldiers away from it walk there, and a unit walks toward an independent we cannot befriend yet (stopping 2 tiles away). A settlement within 6 tiles of a village at war with you, with no soldier on or next to it, buys one with the gold above the reserve. One melee unit as strong as the best you can train is always kept: every settlement centre defends at the full strength of the strongest melee unit you trained, bought or upgraded in this age (20 with none). A threatened or exposed town still growing at population 7 takes the Fort Town Focus, the only way a town can buy walls, and then buys them. All defenders stay below 4 per settlement; the advisor's military units are only trained below 2 per settlement. While your gold income is below zero, no unit is added except defenders of a threatened settlement, and units are upgraded only there. When a unit shares a tile with another military unit (a new unit from the city), one of them steps to the nearest free tile, your own land first; boxed in by your own soldiers, a neighbour steps out to make room.

A merchant waiting for orders starts the best trade route the game allows, in the trade screen's order (most imported resources first, then the yields it brings by your priority). If the route cannot start where it stands, the merchant walks to that city first. One merchant per city, within each civilization's trade limit.

Spends Influence to befriend independent powers, one a turn (the Influence pays for one): those threatening a settlement first, then those at war with you, then the nearest to your settlements (by their village); one you cannot afford yet keeps the Influence for itself. Once befriending reaches 30, its war with you ends. Under threat, more Influence goes into an ongoing befriending. Also asks civilizations for open borders when your explorers reach their land.

With «Military: shoot or fortify» on. Off (the default) the autopilot only defends: it seeks peace whenever it can. On, in a war someone else started, it retakes a settlement of yours that the enemy holds within 10 tiles of your own: when your settlements are safe and no victory of yours is near, the soldiers the defence leaves free (at least 2 melee, 3 in all, 2 more than the enemy soldiers near it) gather 3 tiles from it with a commander, then ranged and siege units shoot its defences, melee units attack them when the game's preview says it pays, and a soldier occupies each district at 0 health; the settlement taken is kept. While that assault makes progress no white peace is proposed, and a peace that does not give the settlement back is refused; one that does is accepted. The campaign ends when the settlement is yours again, at peace, when your own settlements need the soldiers, after 25 turns or 5 without progress, or when a victory of yours is near. A commander leading it takes Initiative, Mobility and Regiments first, unless it already took a defensive promotion. Never a war of its own, never a settlement that was not yours.

Every turn the autopilot picks the legacy path to steer toward (culture, science or economic; never military): the one this age where you are furthest along and furthest ahead of the best rival you met, with a bonus for your leader's preferred victory and for close triumphs of that kind; it switches only after another path has led for 3 turns, or when the current one is complete (in the final age a completed path is kept: its victory goes on). It then follows that path's priority (Culture, Science or Gold: research and production advice, buildings, policies, growth, purchases); culture also builds one more wonder at a time. Close triumphs of that kind are ticked «Track». Its own work comes first, by age. Research that unlocks the path's work goes first (codex masteries and Literacy; Education and Urban Planning; Currency and Code of Laws; Industrialization and Mass Production). Science: a Library and an Academy in every city for codices (Antiquity); a University in every city and new specialists stacked on the urban tile closest to 40 total yield (Exploration); Launch Pads in your 3 most productive cities (one is needed to win; each runs the repeatable Crewed Space Flight Preparation, 15 Innovation), an Airfield and a Radio Station for the path's projects, a Schoolhouse and a Laboratory in every city, and every project that earns Innovation; once nothing of the path is left to research, the techs and civics that grant Innovation (Modern); cities buy these buildings with gold above the reserve too. Economy: growth onto tiles with a resource and, with «Merchants», merchants while trade routes are open (every age); a Market and a Lighthouse in every city for resource slots (Antiquity); settlers heading for the Distant Lands after Shipbuilding, for treasure convoys (Exploration); a Rail Station, Port, Factory and Stock Exchange in every city, factory resources into the Factories, and the Great Banker opening World Bank offices in other capitals (Modern); towns, then cities, buy these buildings with gold above the reserve, and while the path's techs are still to research the economy keeps science up. Treasure convoys always go home and unload. The tab shows the focus, each path against the best rival, each victory's points against its goal (Innovation, GDP…) and its countdown, the victories switched off in this game, and the close triumphs.

With «Victory focus»: the autopilot plays in phases. Growth (the first quarter of Antiquity, and while settlements are well below the cap; the start of Exploration while towns outnumber cities): food and production weigh most, so towns and cities grow and later build the focus's buildings faster; towns lean to farming. Build-up: the focus's buildings and savings for conversions and the path's buildings; for science and economy no explorers, none of the advisor's soldiers and no Barracks in peace, upgrades only near a threat. Final push (the last age): no new settlers; science banks gold for 3 to 5 Launch Pads before Rocketry and buys them all when it comes. The phase sets the gold reserve and the wonders at once for the turn (your settings stay as they are); the tab shows the phase, its tooltip what it changes. Off: your own settings every turn.

Resources not assigned to any settlement go into free resource slots (the game's resource screen): most valuable by your priority first, cities before towns, only where the game accepts. Assigned resources give their bonuses and count for the economic legacy path and triumphs.

With other leaders, only what the game offers now and your Influence pays for: Counter Spy against a leader whose spy was caught against you (from the Exploration age); Reconciliation with a leader who is Unfriendly or Hostile; one initiative (endeavor) per turn with the leader you stand worst with, the kind that fits your priority first (research collaboration, open markets, cultural exchange, farmers market, local festival, wonder construction), only while no Influence goes to befriending independents; a leader's initiative is supported (not only accepted) when Influence allows. Proposals are never rejected (that would sour the relationship, or mean war). Nothing but the counter-spy while a settlement is threatened; never with a leader at war with you.
